Synopsis:
    Amazon raised £4.25bn in its first-ever sterling bond sale across a four-part deal, part of a broader hyperscaler trend of diversifying funding outside the US to finance AI expansion. Hyperscalers have issued over $200bn in debt in 2026, more than doubling from 2025. Demand, while oversubscribed ~2.5x, was notably weaker than Alphabet's February sterling deal (5x covered), signalling investor appetite for hyperscaler paper is showing early signs of fatigue. The ECB has flagged crowding-out risks in euro bond markets.
